examples.title: Remove room reverberation
examples.inputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.
examples.outputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.
examples.instruction: Remove the room reverberation so the speech sounds dry and clear. Keep the words and voice unchanged.
examples.origin: The wet input is synthesized from the original dry recording. The displayed output is that original dry recording, not a dereverberation-model prediction.
examples.transcriptBasis: Known synthetic source text; signal processing does not change the words.
examples.preservation: Spoken words and source voice; only room reverberation changes.

examples.title: Brighter voice (EQ)

examples.outputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.
examples.instruction: Make the voice brighter by reducing low frequencies and boosting high frequencies. Keep the words and timing unchanged.
examples.origin: Controlled illustration made from the existing synthetic speech with FFmpeg low- and high-shelf filters.
examples.transcriptBasis: Known synthetic source text; signal processing does not change the words.
examples.preservation: Spoken words and timing; only the spectral balance changes.

examples.title: Remove background noise
examples.instruction: Remove the background noise while preserving the words, voice, and timing.
examples.preservation: Spoken words, speaker identity, pitch, and timing.
examples.origin: MUSAN background noise is added to the existing recording for the input. The output is the unmodified original, not a denoising-model prediction; existing ambience in the source is retained.
examples.instructionBasis: Constructed noisy/original pair using a MUSAN background-noise excerpt.
examples.taxonomyBasis: Removing added background-noise contamination while retaining the target content is Acoustic editing.
examples.inputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.
examples.outputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.
examples.transcriptBasis: Known synthetic source text; added noise does not change the words.

examples.title: Phrase replacement
examples.inputText: Do you think the biggest victory is not fighting for what we want, but accepting what we cannot have? In some ways, like I was better equipped to answer that question when I was in my twenty s. Change is going to be a constant. That's such a great question.
examples.outputText: Do you think the biggest victory is not fighting for what we want, and living well with dreams unmet? In some ways, like I was better equipped to answer that question when I was in my twenty s. Change is going to be a constant. That's such a great question.
examples.inputHighlight: but accepting what we cannot have
examples.outputHighlight: and living well with dreams unmet
examples.instruction: Replace “but accepting what we cannot have” with “and living well with dreams unmet”.
examples.sourceLabel: AuK official demo · Content Editing · English
examples.origin: Official Content Editing sample ce-en-2, Replace variant.
examples.transcriptBasis: Official transcript and replacement markers in the project-page sample manifest.
examples.preservation: The requested words change; the speaker and surrounding words are intended to remain consistent.

examples.title: Faster speaking rate
examples.inputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.
examples.outputText: The morning train leaves at nine, and the evening train leaves at six.

mediaPolicy: Official demonstration audio is streamed from the original project pages. Controlled synthetic speech, its FFmpeg acoustic edits, and the two survey-generated SeedAudio speech outputs are stored locally with generation provenance. No blanket audio redistribution license is asserted. Denoising pairs use local MUSAN-noise mixtures as inputs and the unmodified originals as outputs; provenance is recorded in assets/audio/denoising-generation.json.
